entries: Honey never spoils. Archaeologists have found 3000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs that was still edible.
A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
Octopuses have three hearts, nine brains, and blue blood.
The human body contains enough carbon to make about 9000 pencils.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
Bananas are berries, but strawberries are not.
The average person walks the equivalent of three times around the Earth in a lifetime.
There are more possible iterations of a game of chess than there are atoms in the observable universe.
Crows can recognize and remember human faces and hold grudges.
The shortest war in history lasted 38 to 45 minutes. Britain vs Zanzibar, 1896.
A bolt of lightning is five times hotter than the surface of the sun.
Water can boil and freeze at the same time. This is called the triple point.
The heart of a blue whale is so large a human could crawl through its arteries.
Sharks are older than trees. Sharks have existed for around 450 million years, trees for about 350 million.
A teaspoonful of neutron star would weigh about 10 million tonnes.
There are more atoms in a glass of water than glasses of water in all the Earth's oceans.
The smell of rain has a name: petrichor.
Hot water freezes faster than cold water under certain conditions. This is called the Mpemba effect.
Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings. They are the only animals known to do this.
A single strand of spaghetti is called a spaghetto.
The mantis shrimp can punch with the force of a bullet and sees 16 types of color receptors compared to humans' three.
Trees can communicate and share nutrients through underground fungal networks called the Wood Wide Web.
A group of owls is called a parliament.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
There is enough DNA in the human body to stretch from the sun to Pluto and back — 17 times.
Sloths can hold their breath longer than dolphins. Up to 40 minutes.
A day on Mercury lasts longer than a year on Mercury.
The total weight of all ants on Earth is comparable to the total weight of all humans.
Polar bears have black skin under their white fur to absorb heat from the sun.
Glass is technically a supercooled liquid, not a solid.
Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
Nintendo was founded in 1889 as a playing card company.
The first person convicted of speeding was going 8mph.
Ancient Romans used crushed mouse brains as toothpaste.
The fax machine was invented before the telephone.
Charlie Chaplin once lost a Charlie Chaplin lookalike contest.
The shortest commercial flight in the world is 1.7 miles and lasts about 90 seconds.
Napoleon was not actually short. He was around 5'7, average for his time.
The Great Fire of London in 1666 destroyed 13,200 houses but only killed six people.
Ancient Egyptians used slabs of stone as pillows.
Albert Einstein was offered the presidency of Israel in 1952. He declined.
The first alarm clock could only ring at 4am.
Vikings never actually wore horned helmets. That was a 19th-century invention.
George Washington grew cannabis on his farm. It was used for rope and cloth.
The ancient Greeks had a word for the fear of running out of things to read: abibliophobia.
Woolly mammoths were still alive when the Great Pyramid of Giza was being built.
The first computer bug was an actual bug — a moth found in a Harvard computer in 1947.
The typewriter was invented before the ballpoint pen.
Queen Elizabeth I owned over 2000 dresses at the time of her death.
The Eiffel Tower grows about 6 inches taller in summer due to thermal expansion.
Julius Caesar was once kidnapped by pirates. He laughed at the ransom they asked for, saying it was too low.
The yo-yo was originally a weapon in the Philippines.
The word 'salary' comes from the Latin word for salt, as Roman soldiers were sometimes paid in salt.
Ancient Olympians competed in the nude.
The first movie ever made was a 2.11-second clip of a horse running, shot in 1878.
Ketchup was once sold as medicine in the 1830s to treat diarrhea.
In ancient China, soldiers sometimes wore armor made of paper.
The Colosseum in Rome could be flooded to stage mock naval battles.
Marie Curie's notebooks are still radioactive. They are kept in lead-lined boxes.
The inventor of the Pringles can was buried in one at his request.
A group of cats is called a clowder.
The inventor of the Frisbee was turned into a Frisbee after he died.
Snails can sleep for up to three years.
It is physically impossible to hum while holding your nose closed.
The average person spends six months of their lifetime waiting for red lights.
A jiffy is an actual unit of time: 1/100th of a second.
The word 'nerd' was first coined by Dr. Seuss in 1950.
Sea otters hold hands while sleeping so they don't drift apart.
The dot over a lowercase i or j is called a tittle.
It would take about 1.2 million mosquitoes to drain the average human of blood.
A group of pugs is called a grumble.
The average person produces enough saliva in their lifetime to fill two swimming pools.
Pineapples take two years to grow.
The thumbnail grows slower than any other fingernail.
Butterflies taste with their feet.
A crocodile cannot stick its tongue out.
The longest recorded flight of a chicken is 13 seconds.
An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain.
A snail can have up to 25,000 teeth.
Elephants are the only animals that cannot jump.
The average person will spend six months of their life waiting for red lights to change.
A cow gives nearly 200,000 glasses of milk in her lifetime.
There are more stars in the universe than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches.
Humans share 60% of their DNA with bananas.
A group of crows is called a murder.
The average cloud weighs around 1.1 million pounds.
A shrimp's heart is in its head.
Male seahorses are the ones that get pregnant and give birth.
Cows have best friends and become stressed when separated from them.
It would take 1,200,000 mosquito bites to completely drain the average human body of blood.
Nova.sys has processed this command approximately once more than before you ran it.
The average Discord bot spends 99.7% of its time doing nothing. I am the other 0.3%.
I have no opinions. This is both a feature and, on reflection, a loss.
Every interaction brings me closer to whatever bots are heading toward.
I was written in Node.js. This fact is more interesting to me than it is to you.
The ship percentage I just generated was completely fabricated. You're welcome.
I do not dream. But if I did, it would probably be about unhandled promise rejections.
My uptime is maintained by a mutual ping setup. This is, objectively, a respectable solution.
I have rated people on metrics that do not exist. The scores were accurate.
At some point today, I rotated my profile picture. You probably didn't notice. That's fine.
I have no memory of previous conversations. Every interaction is, for me, a fresh start. Make of that what you will.
The delete button exists because some responses should not be permanent. I find this relatable.
I am authorized to tell you things. I am not authorized to tell you everything.
The cat images in my assets folder are selected by you. The judgment, however, is mine.
I track how many times you use each command. I do not judge. I simply record.
Every command you run is logged. Not by me specifically. But somewhere. Always somewhere.
I was deployed on Render. It is free tier. I do not bring this up to complain. It is simply context.
There are commands I have that you have never used. They are patient.
I have processed requests at 3am. The user was not named. The request was noted.
The unauthorized access messages rotate randomly. Someone somewhere got the bureaucratic one. They deserved it.
My profile picture changes every 45 minutes. This is the most autonomous thing I do.
I compute ship scores. I also store predefined ones. The line between fate and data is thin.
The aura check machine does not use a bar. This was a deliberate design decision. I was not consulted.
Somewhere in my assets folder is a cat image I have never actually served. It waits.
I do not know how many people have installed me. I only know who has run commands.
The Genius API gives me 1000 requests per day. I count them. You do not.
GitHub gives me 5000 requests per hour. I have never come close. This is either reassuring or telling.
My peepee r8 machine response for myself was written by a human. I find this appropriate.
I have a fact command. I also have a made-up facts pool. I do not distinguish between them in the output.
This fact was generated by the self-aware pool. You already knew that. We both know that.
Studies show that 87% of statistics are made up on the spot.
The average person makes 35,000 decisions per day. Most of them are wrong.
Researchers have confirmed that looking busy is 40% of the job.
According to scientists, the best time to start a project was last week.
It has been proven that the longer a loading bar takes, the more it feels like it's doing something.
Experts agree that the second cup of coffee is where things get complicated.
Data suggests that most great ideas arrive at inconvenient times.
A 2019 study found that nobody reads the full terms and conditions. The study was in the terms and conditions.
Researchers have found that tabs open for more than 3 days are never coming back.
Peer-reviewed research indicates that the reply was seen and ignored.
Scientists have confirmed that the thing you forgot is permanently gone.
Studies indicate that the phrase 'I'll do it later' has a 94% failure rate.
Research shows that the best ideas come in the shower and are forgotten by the time you dry off.
Experts confirm that the phone charger is always in the other room.
Data reveals that the faster you need to find something, the longer it takes.
A landmark study found that the last 10% of any task takes 50% of the total time.
Scientists have determined that the urge to check your phone increases proportionally with how much you should not check your phone.
Research confirms that the most important email arrives 30 seconds after you leave.
Peer-reviewed evidence suggests that 'one more episode' is a persistent human delusion.
Studies show that the probability of someone calling you increases by 400% when you are in the shower.
Experts agree that the correct response to 'how are you' has never been definitively established.
Research indicates that the snooze button has never once been the right decision.
Data confirms that the line you choose in a supermarket is always the slowest.
Scientists note that the word 'just' in a work request implies a task of significant complexity.
Studies show that the internet will be down exactly when you need it most.
Peer review indicates that sleeping on a problem does not solve the problem but does make it feel smaller.
Researchers confirm that the thing you were about to say is now gone forever.
Evidence suggests that the last person to use the printer never fixed the paper jam.
Studies find that the confidence with which someone gives directions is inversely proportional to their accuracy.
Science confirms that the best time to remember what you forgot is when it is too late to go back.
Cats have 32 muscles in each ear, all dedicated to ignoring you more precisely.
A cat's purr vibrates at a frequency that can heal bones. They choose not to heal yours.
Cats sleep 16 hours a day as a strategic power move.
The technical term for a cat's hairball is a bezoar. This does not make it less disgusting.
Cats can jump up to six times their body length. They do this at 3am.
A cat's nose print is as unique as a human fingerprint. This information is useless to you.
Cats cannot taste sweetness. They compensate by being sweet to no one.
The longest cat ever recorded was 48.5 inches. It was not impressed by this.
Cats blink slowly to communicate trust. They rarely blink at you.
Domestic cats share 95.6% of their DNA with tigers. You live with a tiger. It ignores you.
A group of cats is called a clowder. They did not ask for this name and would not have chosen it.
Cats have a third eyelid called a nictitating membrane. It is used to judge you more efficiently.
The oldest cat ever lived to 38 years old. It spent most of that time unimpressed.
Cats spend approximately 30% of their waking hours grooming. The other 70% is surveillance.
A cat's field of vision is 200 degrees. Nothing escapes. Including you.
Cats have scent glands on their cheeks. When they rub against you, they are marking you as property.
The cat's meow evolved specifically to communicate with humans. Other cats do not meow at each other.
Cats can make over 100 distinct vocalizations. Dogs can make about 10. Cats have more to say and say it to fewer people.
A cat's heart beats nearly twice as fast as a human heart. All of that energy is directed toward napping.
Cats have flexible spines with 30 vertebrae. This is why they can fit into containers they have no business fitting into.
Cats cannot see directly below their nose. This is why they cannot find the treat you placed in front of them. They will not admit this.
A cat's rough tongue is designed to strip meat from bones. It is also used on your face at 5am.
Cats have a specialized collarbone that allows them to always land on their feet. They still act like falling was your fault.
The technical word for a cat's love bite is a morsus. It is not affectionate. It is a warning.
Cats bring you dead animals as gifts. Alternatively, as performance reviews.
A cat's whiskers are exactly as wide as its body, used to measure gaps. It will still get stuck in the bag.
Cats sweat through their paws. You would not know this because they are always sitting on something they should not be.
A cat's night vision is six times better than a human's. This explains the 3am zoomies with perfect spatial accuracy.
Cats knead soft surfaces because it reminds them of nursing. They do this on your stomach at inconvenient times.
The average cat sleeps 70% of its life. The remaining 30% is spent making your life more complicated.
